_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FN.5] What a brew shows, and the marks a culture left in its temple (Mike, 10 Oct, design §FN). Claude (chat) wrote it; nothing reads it yet, and Claude Code removes this prefix as each block is wired (queues 82 and 83). 'mike' lines are his words; 'from_research' lines are what two quick searches and general knowledge gave, not his; 'look' lines are Claude's first guesses for Claude Code to tune by eye and Mike to settle by playing. Use lines describe rites only: no doses and no preparation. It is additive and reads nothing in data/brew.json, whose placeholder tint stands until queue 83.
_help.rule: The filter is what you see, not light and not a game rule: see rule.kept_inside.
_help.evidence: Each plant's from_research names its sources and how strong the evidence is. Trip reports are anecdotes. Treat every look as a direction.
_help.marks: Real marks each people left, not invented runes (Mike). Several roster cultures had no writing, so 'kind' says what they did leave. All of it is Claude's general knowledge, unsourced here: check before the ruin is built (confidence 'general').

rule.kind: visual filter, unique per culture, one shared idea across ruins (Mike)
does: glyph animations that change in trippy ways
rule.tells: the hidden carvings tell a hidden story of the ancient people's history
rule.acts_where: in the ruin, where the glyphs are; drunk at the shaman's hearth (§FM.7)

kept_inside.no_hallucinations: the carvings are really there and sober eyes miss them; the filter adds no creatures, faces or other things that are not in the ruin (§FM.3)
kept_inside.glow_is_not_light: the glow casts no light, does not count toward a floor's lit test (§FF.2) and does not touch the boss or the dark (look rule: only things that give off light glow)
kept_inside.gates_nothing: no gameplay number changes while it runs; no timer on anything else, no torch drain (§FM.3, §FM.7)
kept_inside.never_harder: a different experience for each plant, never a harder mode (§FM.7); sacred datura 'not going to be more dangerous' (Mike)
kept_inside.respect: the shaman teaches the respectful harvest (§FM.7); peyote is IUCN Vulnerable

duration.open: may be short for reading glyphs (§FN.8 call 6)

aztec.plant_source: data/sacred/sacred_plants.json, id teonanacatl (its ruin field there still says maya; the roster gave it to the Maya as 'shared')
aztec.mike: I think the Aztecs are more focused on the mushrooms
aztec.replaces: ololiuhqui, which brew.json and queue 72 grow as a liana; whether it stays as a second Aztec plant: open
aztec.grows_where: cloud forest and wet meadow in the data; the desert surface cannot grow it honestly (§FN.8 call 1)

marks.kind: pictographic writing: day-sign glyphs, rebus signs, codex-style figures

reports: kaleidoscopic and geometric patterns that move
sources: Teonanacatl (Ancient Origins and a species page)
from_research.evidence: snippets of several pages; general knowledge for 'breathing' surfaces

aztec.look: the glyphs multiply and animate, geometry breathes across the stone; the largest palette swap of the set

inca.mike: the Incan people would be San Pedro

marks.kind: no script: knotted cords (khipu) and woven or painted geometric patterns (tocapu)

reports: heightened sensitivity to light and colour
geometric patterns, open and closed-eye visuals
sources: San Pedro: Everything You Need To Know
from_research.evidence: snippets of several pages; 'warm, grounded' is general lore, not from a page opened

inca.look: the carved marks saturate and glow; a gentler reveal than the mushroom's, the world turned up rather than changed

marks.kind: no script: rock art and the patterns of shamans' drums and carved bone

reports: calm and drowsy at first, then dreamlike
objects seeming very large or very small
from_research.evidence: one page opened in full; a deliriant (muscimol), not a classic psychedelic

taiga.look: scale and proportion warp, the stone swells and shrinks, soft and woozy; no phantom creatures

maya.plant_status: open: the roster gave the Maya the mushroom as 'shared with the Aztec', and Mike has named it the Aztec's (§FN.8 call 2)

marks.kind: a full script: logosyllabic glyph blocks
no script: yarn paintings and offering discs in the Wixarika tradition
no script: petroglyphs and painted rock art
no script: geoglyph earthworks and rock art
no script: patterned dry-stone walls and carved soapstone birds

gulf_swamp.plant_status: not chosen (the roster's candidate is yaupon, a mild stimulant)

marks.kind: no script: engraved shell and copper iconography of the Mississippian peoples

bhang.why: India is not on the compass (data/ruin_compass.json)

reports: faint patterns and textures, once pixel- or grid-like (one trip report)
sources: a trip-report article on bhang in India
